ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small disk is at rest on a tablecloth, located at the center of the horizontal surface of a square table. One edge of the tablecloth coincides with the edge \( AB \) of the table, as shown in the figure. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the disk and the tablecloth is \( \mu_{1} \), and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the disk and the table surface is \( \mu_{2} \). The tablecloth is suddenly pulled away from the table with a constant acceleration \( a \), where the direction of the acceleration is horizontal and perpendicular to the edge \( AB \). (Let \( g \) denote the acceleration due to gravity.)

1. If the disk does not fall off the table in the end, what condition does the acceleration $a$ satisfy?

One edge of the tablecloth coincides with the edge \(AB\) of the table, as shown in the figure. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the disk and the tablecloth is \(\mu_1\), and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the disk and the table surface is \(\mu_2\). If the disk does not fall off the table in the end, what condition must the acceleration \(a\) satisfy?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a perspective view of a square tabletop. The left table edge is labeled A and B, and a small disk is drawn near the center of the tabletop. A tablecloth covers the tabletop, and one of its edges coincides with the table edge AB; on the right side, the shape of the tablecloth being pulled out to the right is drawn, and a horizontal arrow labels acceleration a, indicating that the tablecloth is pulled away in the direction perpendicular to AB. Reasoning: Let the side length of the square table be L, and take the x-axis perpendicular to AB and along the direction of pulling the tablecloth. The disk is initially at the center of the tabletop, so its distance to the far edge ahead from which it may fall is L/2, and at the same time its initial coordinate relative to AB is also L/2. When the disk is still on the tablecloth, the tablecloth moves relative to the ground with acceleration a; the disk is acted on by the kinetic friction force from the tablecloth, and its acceleration along the pulling direction is μ1 g. Therefore, starting from rest, at time t the displacement of the edge of the tablecloth that originally coincided with AB is (1/2) a t^2, and the displacement of the disk is (1/2) μ1 g t^2. When the tablecloth edge catches up with the disk, their relative displacement equals the disk's initial distance from AB, L/2: (1/2)(a-μ1 g)t^2 = L/2, so t^2 = L/(a-μ1 g). This also requires a>μ1 g; the final obtained condition will automatically satisfy this. At the instant of leaving the tablecloth, the disk has already moved forward s1 = (1/2) μ1 g t^2, and its velocity is v1 = μ1 g t. Then the disk slides on the exposed tabletop, acted on only by the kinetic friction force from the tabletop to decelerate it, with deceleration magnitude μ2 g. Therefore the distance it continues to slide on the tabletop until stopping is s2 = v1^2/(2 μ2 g). In order that the disk finally not fall from the far edge, the total displacement from the initial center position cannot exceed L/2: s1+s2 ≤ L/2. Substituting t^2=L/(a-μ1 g): (1/2)μ1 g·L/(a-μ1 g) + (μ1^2 g^2·L/(a-μ1 g))/(2 μ2 g) ≤ L/2. Simplifying gives L/[2(a-μ1 g)] · [μ1 g + μ1^2 g/μ2] ≤ L/2, namely μ1 g(1+μ1/μ2) ≤ a-μ1 g. Therefore a ≥ μ1 g(2+μ1/μ2).
